conventions.convention: The channel and pipe use x as the axial coordinate. Channel shear values are fixed-coordinate stress components, not oriented wall tractions. Pipe uniqueness requires C² regularity on the full cross-sectional disk, including its axis.
The vortex excludes the entire z-axis. Positive circular orientation is given by (R cos θ, R sin θ, z₀), with increasing θ; circulation is 2πκ.

The sphere resultant uses n=x/a pointing from the sphere center into the exterior, opposite to the exterior fluid domain's inner-boundary outward normal. Exterior Stokes uniqueness assumes ACω, uniform directional decay and pressure normalization at infinity.

The wall-layer claim is classical only for t>0 and y>0, excluding the initial-wall corner. The separate torus equations and circulation are defined through periodic Euclidean lifts; translating a loop lift by a period-lattice vector preserves circulation.

Enthalpy is h(q)=∫ from ρref to q of P′(r)/r dr. Bernoulli constancy across a connected component requires steady fields and zero curl; Kelvin conservation requires the stated closed material-loop and mixed-derivative regularity.
The inviscid constant-density incompressible branch has pressure stress σE=−pI₃ and imposes no boundary condition or solution-existence assertion.
The potential-sphere boundary condition is impermeable slip, generally with nonzero tangential velocity. Its zero resultant is pressure-only and uses the sphere normal pointing into the exterior.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated classical positive-density barotropic Euler system with C² pressure law and time-independent C² conservative potential, steady Bernoulli is constant along streamlines and throughout connected curl-free components; circulation is constant for closed material loops with the stated regularity. Independently, every C² vector field satisfies (v·∇)v=∇(|v|²/2)−v×curl v.
The formal constant-density incompressible Euler system is ∂tu+(u·∇)u+ρ₀⁻¹∇p=0 and div u=0, with the stated classical regularity and constant ρ₀>0; its pressure stress is σE=−pI₃.

Assuming ACω, the displayed exterior sphere fields solve steady Stokes, have zero boundary velocity and uniform far-field velocity U, give the oriented resultant 6πμaU, and are unique among classical pairs with the same data and uniform bounds u−U=O(r⁻¹), ∇u=O(r⁻²), p−p∞=O(r⁻²).

The displayed positive-time half-space diffusion layer solves unsteady Stokes and Navier–Stokes, has the stated wall and initial limits, and satisfies the Gaussian tail bound. Separately, the specified periodic sine shear and material loop have circulation Γ(t)=AcCα exp(−νk²t), with Cα>0 for 0<α<π.

Within the stated channel and full-disk radial pipe ansätze, the unique profiles are v(y)=V₀+(V₁−V₀)y/h+Gy(h−y)/(2μ) and w(r)=G(a²−r²)/(4μ), with the displayed fluxes and channel shear components; both solve stationary Navier–Stokes and steady Stokes exactly.

The punctured-axis vortex has zero curl but circulation 2πκ≠0 and no single-valued C¹ global potential. The separate solid-rotation solution has Bernoulli quantity p₀/ρ₀+Ω₀²r², constant along streamlines but different at distinct radii. Both displayed fields solve the stated constant-density equation for every ν>0.

The displayed exterior sphere potential and pressure give a smooth steady incompressible Euler solution with uniform far-field limits, impermeable slip boundary condition, and zero pressure-only resultant with normal n=x/a.
